published.citation: Kammer et al. 2015, dayside brightness temperature at 3.6 µm (NASA Exoplanet Archive emission table): 1213 +/- 62 K, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...810..118K/abstract

temperature.note: Its day side's brightness temperature is measured in secondary eclipse at 3.6 µm (Spitzer Space Telescope satellite Infrared Array Camera (IRAC)) and nobody has imaged it, so the colour is a Planck spectrum at its published temperature.
temperature.chosen: 2 measured of 2 rows; the smallest relative uncertainty, then the longest wavelength
temperature.facility: Spitzer Space Telescope satellite Infrared Array Camera (IRAC)
